title: Protocol for identifying physiologically relevant binding proteins of G-protein-coupled receptors
protocol: Culture and maintain HEK293 cells in 15-cm dishes in EMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 37°C in a humidified CO2 (5%) incubator.
Seed HEK293 cells (∼8 × 10^6 cells) in 15-cm dishes and incubate the cells at 37°C in a CO2 incubator for 16–20 h.
Dilute 5 μg of GPR110, or F663S, or M45 plasmid in 700 μL of Opti-MEM I Reduced Serum Media (Opti-MEM).
Dilute 50 μL Lipofectamine 2000 in 700 μL of Opti-MEM.
Mix solutions from steps above and incubate for 15 min at room temperature (25°C).
Add the mixed solution to the 15-cm dish of cells using a pipette.
Gently rock the dish back and forth.
Incubate the cells at 37°C under 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Replace the medium with PBS.
Remove and discard the medium by aspiration.
Wash cells with 10 mL PBS.
Add 10 mL PBS gently to the side of the dish, rocking it back and forth 3–5 times.
Aspiration should be performed gently.
Remove and discard the PBS by aspiration.
Add 5 mL PBS.
Prepare freshly 200 mM DSS in DMSO.
Add 25 μL of 200 mM DSS to cells in PBS.
Gently rock the dish back and forth 3–5 times.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature (25°C).
Add 150 μL of 1M Tris-HCl buffer (pH = 7.4) to quench the crosslinking reaction.
Mix gently by rocking the dish back and forth several times.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Harvest cells.
Detach the cells without removing PBS using a cell lifter.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15-mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 4°C at 1,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant by aspiration.
Add 1.5 mL cold lysis buffer to the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down 3–5 times.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 1.5 Eppendorf tube.
Incubate the cell suspension on ice for 30 min.
Vortex for 1–2 s every 5 min.
Centrifuge the cells for 15 min at 4°C at 15,000 × g.
Collect and transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube.
Keep samples on ice.
Determine the protein concentration using BCA Protein Assay kit.
Adjust the protein concentration to the lowest sample concentration with lysis buffer if necessary.
Incubate the lysate with HA antibody.
Transfer 1.3 mL of the lysate for each sample to an Eppendorf tube.
Add 40 μL of HA antibody to the lysate.
Incubate samples on a rotator overnight at 4°C.
Prepare protein G beads.
Add 40 μL of well-resuspended magnetic Dynabeads Protein G to a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Place the tube in the rack of DynaMag-2 magnet for 1 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Transfer the HA antibody-incubated lysate to the tube containing the Dynabeads Protein G.
Incubate for 4 h at 4°C on a rotator.
Place samples in the rack of DynaMag-2 magnet for 1 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Wash beads by adding 800 μL of lysis buffer.
Gently shake the tubes by hand.
Spin down the beads briefly using a low-speed microcentrifuge.
Place the tubes on the magnet for 1 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing steps two more times.
Remove the supernatant with a pipette while the tubes are on a magnet rack.
Add 50 μL of 1 mg/mL HA peptide to each tube from Step 5div.
Place the samples on a rotisserie rotator for 20 min at 30°C.
Place the samples on DynaMag-2 magnet for 1 min.
Collect and transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube.
Mix 40 μL of the protein solution with 13.3 μL 4x lithium dodecyl sulfate (LDS) sample buffer containing 5% β-mercaptoethanol.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 30 min.
Assemble a XCell SureLock Mini-Cell system with NuPAGE 4%-12% Bis-Tris mini gel and MOPS SDS running buffer.
Load 45 μL of each sample.
Load 5 μL protein standards before the first sample and after the last sample.
Start electrophoresis with a constant voltage of 200 V.
Stop electrophoresis when the dye front is about 1 cm from the base of the gel.
Stain the gel with Coomassie G-250.
Wash the gel with ultrapure water for three 5-minute intervals.
Incubate the gel in SimplyBlue SafeStain (Coomassie G-250) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Remove and discard the staining solution after incubation.
Incubate the gel in ultrapure water for 1 hour.
Cut out gel bands using a wide stainless steel surgical prep blade.
Clean gel cutting tools with methanol and water subsequently.
Clean the workspace (glass plates and bench) thoroughly.
Dice the gel slice of each lane into 1 × 1 mm pieces using a single edge razor blade.
Collect the gel pieces into a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube containing 200 μL water using filter forceps.
Remove and discard water from the tube using a gel loading tip.
Add 200 μL of de-staining solution to cover the gel pieces.
Vortex and spin briefly with a low-speed microcentrifuge.
Incubate samples in a shaker for 30 min at room temperature (25°C).
Remove and discard the supernatant using a gel loading tip.
Repeat Steps i-ii.
Add 50 μL 100% ACN to dehydrate the gel pieces.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate on a shaker for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Dry the gel pieces completely with a vacuum concentrator (typically 30 min at 25°C).
Add 100 μL of 10 mM DTT freshly made in 25 mM NH4HCO3 to the dried gel pieces.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate the samples at 56°C for 1 h.
Add 100 μL of 110 mM iodoacetamide freshly made in 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate at room temperature (25°C) for 45 min in the dark.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Add 200 μL of 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate on a shaker for 10 min.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Add 200 μL 25 mM NH4HCO3 in 50% ACN.
Incubate on a shaker for 10 min.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Repeat Steps vi-vii.
Add 50 μL 100% ACN to dehydrate the gel pieces.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate on a shaker for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Dry the gel pieces completely with a vacuum concentrator (typically 30 min at 25°C).
Prepare freshly 12.5 ng/μL trypsin/Lys-C in 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Add 100 μL of 12.5 ng/μL trypsin to dried gel pieces.
Incubate on ice for 30 min to allow absorption of the solution into the gel.
Incubate the samples at 37°C in an incubator for 16–20 h.
Prepare peptide extraction solution (PXS).
Mix 5% formic acid in water with ACN at a 1:1 ratio.
Add 100 μL of PXS to the sample.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate in a shaker for 10 min at room temperature.
Collect and transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Add 100 μL of PXS to the gel pieces.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Incubate in a shaker for 10 min at room temperature.
Collect and pool the supernatant with the previous supernatant.
Repeat the incubation, collection, and pooling steps as necessary.
Dry the pooled supernatant containing tryptic peptides with a vacuum concentrator (typically 2–3 h at 25°C).
Dissolve dried peptides by adding 10 μL of 0.1% TFA.
Vortex and spin briefly.
Check the pH of the peptide solution using a pH paper; ensure it is less than 4 before proceeding to desalting.
Remove salts and contaminants using Millipore C18 ZipTip according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute purified peptides with 10 μL 0.1% TFA in 50% ACN.
Dry purified peptides to dryness with a vacuum concentrator at 25°C for typically 30 minutes.
Reconstitute peptide samples by adding 5 μL of 0.1% TFA to each dried desalted peptide sample.
Vortex the reconstituted peptide samples for 10 seconds.
Spin down the vortexed samples briefly with a microcentrifuge.
Transfer the samples into vials compatible with the autosampler of the liquid chromatography system.
Set the temperature of the autosampler to 4°C.
Select LC-MS/MS method, injection volume (e.g., 2 μL), vial position, etc.
Run sequence.
Inject peptides onto a C18 peptide trap column and wash with 25 μL of trap column LC solvent at a rate of 5 μL/min for 5 min.
Elute peptides from the trap column into an analytical column.
Separate peptides using 120-min gradients of nano-LC Mobile Phase B at a rate of 300 nL/min.
Analyze nano-LC eluent by high resolution mass spectrometry in full scan mode and MS/MS in data-dependent acquisition mode (DDA).
Identify proteins by searching MS/MS data against NCBInr database.
Compare binding proteins of GPR110 with the M45 control to identify potential interacting proteins.
Process batches of raw files for GPR110- and M45-transfected samples using Mascot (v2.3.2, Matrix Science).
Search for protein identification using Mascot against the NCBInr database.
Set enzyme to trypsin.
Set precursor ion mass tolerance to 10 ppm.
Set fragment ion mass tolerance to 0.3 Da.
Allow up to 2 missed cleavages.
Fix carbamidomethyl modification of cysteine residues.
Include oxidation of methionine as a variable modification.
Add 156.07864 Da on lysine or N-terminal for end-capping modification.
Filter results with a false positive threshold of 1% and an expect value less than 0.05.
Calculate the expect score using either homology or significance threshold.
Export search results to Excel files.
Compare proteins identified from GPR110-transfected samples with those from M45 controls.
Identify potential interacting proteins of GPR110.
Exclude non-specific binding proteins found in M45 samples.
Exclude proteins not reproducible in three independent experiments.
Open Progenesis QI for Proteomics.
Create an “LC-MS Experiment” for a gel fraction (e.g., Fraction A, B or C).
Name the experiment (e.g., Fraction A).
Select “Profile data” as Data type.
Select “High resolution mass spectrometer” as Machine type.
Select Experiment folder.
Click on "Create experiment".
Import data.
Import raw mass spectrometric files of the fraction (e.g., A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, and A6).
Start automatic processing.
Select “Assess all runs in the experiment for suitability” in “Select an alignment reference” box.
Select “yes” in “Automatic alignment” box.
Select “perform peak picking” in “Peak picking” box.
Select “Relative Quantitation using non-conflicting peptides” in “Protein Quantitation” box.
Review alignment.
Exclude features with charge of 1 and charge > 7 for the analysis.
Set up experiment design.
Create new experiment design (e.g., WT vs. KO).
Set up conditions (e.g., group A1, A2 and A3 as “WT” and group A4, A5 and A6 as “KO”).
Select “Export as mgf file” under the “Identify peptides” window.
Search for protein identification using Mascot (v2.3.2, Matrix Science) against the NCBInr human database.
Export Mascot results to xml files.
Import the xml result files under the “Identify peptides” window.
Save the processed data for the “Experiment” (e.g., Fraction A).
Repeat Steps 10a-10i for each fraction (e.g., Fractions B and C).
Combine processed data.
Import processed Experiments for each fraction.
Recombine processed Experiments for all fractions from each sample.
Combine runs from each fraction from the same sample.
Setup experimental design (e.g., WT vs. F663S).
Export protein quantitation data to Excel.
Analyze data.
Obtain the ratio of binding protein over GPR110 for WT GPR110- and F663S-transfected samples, for each or selected potential interacting protein identified from Step 9.
Calculate p value using Student’s test.
Identify physiologically relevant partners.
Validate occludin as GPR110 interacting partner by reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation assay.
Prepare cell lysate.
Culture and transfect HEK293 cells with WT GPR110, F663S mutant, or empty vector M45 as described in Steps 1–2.
Remove and discard medium after 24 h transfection.
Add 10 mL PBS to the culture dish.
Gently rock the culture dish back and forth.
Remove and discard PBS.
Repeat Step iii.
Add 1.5 mL lysis buffer to the cells.
Scrape with a cell lifter.
Transfer the cell suspension into an Eppendorf tube.
Take 60 μL of each lysate.
Add 20 μL 4x lithium dodecyl sulfate (LDS) sample buffer containing 5% β-mercaptoethanol to each lysate.
Vortex and spin the samples.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 30 min.
Split 1.3 mL of each lysate into two Eppendorf tubes.
Add 20 μL HA antibody or 20 μL occludin antibody to each tube.
Proceed with immunoprecipitation procedure as described in Steps 5b-5d.
Elute the co-immunoprecipitated proteins by adding 40 μL 2x lithium dodecyl sulfate (LDS) sample buffer containing 2.5% β-mercaptoethanol to each tube.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 30 min.
Place tubes in the rack of DynaMag-2 magnet for 1 min.
Collect and transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube.
The samples are ready for western blotting described below.
Assemble the XCell SureLock Mini-Cell system.
Place 10- or 15-well NuPAGE 4%-12% Bis-Tris mini gels in the system.
Load 5 μL protein markers into the gel wells.
Sequentially load 15 μL of pre-IP lysate samples (M45, WT, and F663S).
Sequentially load 15 μL of HA-IP samples (M45, WT, and F663S).
Sequentially load 15 μL of occludin-IP samples (M45, WT, and F663S).
Load an additional 5 μL protein markers.
Start electrophoresis at a constant voltage of 200 V.
Stop electrophoresis when the dye front is about 1 cm from the base of the gel.
Carefully remove the precast gel from the XCell SureLock Mini-Cell system.
Assemble the transfer blot “sandwich” in the Trans-Blot Turbo transfer cassette.
Place a Trans-Blot Turbo Mini 0.2 μm PVDF Transfer Pack into the cassette.
Start transferring proteins to PVDF membrane at a constant voltage of 25 V for 30 min.
Remove the PVDF membrane from the cassette.
Block the membrane with TBST containing 5% skim milk for 1 hour at room temperature (25°C).
Wash the membrane in TBST 3 times with agitation for 5 min each.
Cut the membrane according to the molecular weight of target proteins.
Incubate the membrane slices in 5 mL of respective primary antibody diluted in TBST containing 5% BSA overnight (16–20 h) at 4°C on a low-speed shaker.
Remove the primary antibody solution.
Wash the membrane in TBST 3 times with agitation for 5 min each.
Incubate the membranes in peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibody diluted in TBST containing 5% milk with agitation for 1 h at room temperature (25°C).
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Wash the membrane in TBST 3 times with agitation for 5 min each.
Incubate the membrane with ECL Substrate reagent for 5 min.
Visualize the protein bands using an imager.
Optional: Reprobe the bottom membrane with β-actin.
Wash the membrane with TBST for 5 min.
Incubate the membrane in 20 mL of stripping buffer (Restore western blot stripping buffer, Thermo Scientific) with agitation for 15 min at room temperature (25°C).
Wash the membrane in TBST 3 times with agitation for 5 min each.
Block the membrane with TBST containing 5% skim milk with agitation for 30 min at room temperature (25°C).
Wash the membrane in TBST three times with agitation for 5 minutes each.
Incubate the membrane in 5 mL of β-actin antibody diluted in TBST containing 5% BSA overnight (16–20 hours) at 4°C on a low-speed shaker.
Confirm occludin is co-immunoprecipitated with WT GPR110, but not with the M45 control.
Confirm WT GPR110 is co-immunoprecipitated with occludin, but not with the M45.
Quantify band intensity using appropriate software.
Calculate the ratio of co-immunoprecipitated occludin over the bait GPR110.
Compare the ratio of WT GPR110 transfected-sample with that of the F663S-transfected sample.
Calculate the ratio of co-immunoprecipitated GPR110 over the bait occludin.
Compare the ratio of WT GPR110 transfected-sample with that of the F663S-transfected sample.
Note: The ratio of the prey protein over the bait protein is expected to decrease for the F663S-transfected sample compared to the WT sample.
Use data from pre-IP lysate for normalization of the bait protein.
